# FoxIO JA4 reference fixtures

Each `.hex` file is the raw TCP payload (hex-encoded, one line) of a single
TLS ClientHello record - i.e. it includes the 5-byte TLS record header,
which `foxio_reference_test.go` strips before calling `ParseClientHello`.

Extracted from official test pcaps in the upstream
[FoxIO-LLC/ja4](https://github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4) repository, commit
`0e54bc8371de34df94a35f2442c05bda2e8b2034` (2026-06-19), using:

```
tshark -r pcap/<file> -Y "tls.handshake.type==1[&& tcp.stream==N]" -T fields -e tcp.payload
```

Expected `JA4.1` values (asserted in the Go test) come from that repo's own
checked-in expected output at `python/test/testdata/<file>.json`, which is
generated by FoxIO's reference implementation (`python/ja4.py`, which
itself shells out to `tshark`) and diffed in their own CI
(`python/test/test_ja4_output.py`) - i.e. this is FoxIO's own ground truth,
not a re-derivation.

| File                            | Source pcap                    | stream | Notes                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `foxio_tls12.hex`                 | `pcap/tls12.pcap`                | 0      | Real browser capture, TLS 1.3 via supported_versions          |
| `foxio_tls_non_ascii_alpn.hex`    | `pcap/tls-non-ascii-alpn.pcapng` | 0      | First ALPN protocol is 2 raw non-ASCII bytes (`0xba 0xad`)     |
| `foxio_tls_alpn_h2.hex`           | `pcap/tls-alpn-h2.pcap`          | 0      | 46 cipher suites, explicit `h2` ALPN, non-GREASE reserved sig-alg codes (`efef`/`eeee`/`eded`) |
| `foxio_https3_301_get.hex`        | `pcap/https3-301-get.pcap`       | 0      | TLS 1.0, SNI is the *only* extension and there's no signature_algorithms extension - exercises the empty-JA4_c-input case |
| `foxio_tls_sni_stream0.hex`       | `pcap/tls-sni.pcapng`            | 0      | Chrome to `clientservices.googleapis.com`; same domain as the non-ASCII-ALPN fixture but a genuinely different capture (confirmed via diff, not just visual inspection - see commit history) |

Tooling note: `tshark` isn't a project dependency - it was used only in this
one-time, local extraction step to avoid writing a pcap/pcapng parser (or
adding a pcap-parsing Go dependency) just to prepare test fixtures.
